text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Elias Hrawi talks about Israeli contacts with Lebanese opposition abroad.
- Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri holds talks with Britain's Tony Blair which covered the Middle East peace process, regional issues and Lebanon's reconstruction plans.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright takes a vacation without taking a stand on the travel ban to Lebanon.
- Pragmatic president explains why Iraqis were refused entry to the Pan Arab Games in Beirut, saying it was not worth upsetting Gulf states for a few exports to Baghdad.
- Clinton administration will try to get Syria exempted from legislation that prohibits U.S. citizens from doing business with nations that condone terrorism.
- Travel ban to be lifted? U.S. State Department allows American citizens to attend Beirut conference.
- Israel's proxy South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia agrees to open up a second crossing point between the zone it controls in south Lebanon and the rest of the country.
- Lebanon wins two gold medals and one bronze in the Pan Arab Games in Beirut.
- The Vatican pressures Washington to lift the travel ban on Lebanon.
